items.title: AI agents can form political camps—and changing their conversation partners does little to soften their views
items.excerpt: In a Nature Communications experiment, LLM agents given political positions and free to choose their contacts split into opposing camps that increasingly preferred their own company; rewiring their partners did little to soften views.

items.title: Machine learning reveals potential warning signal for polar vortex disruptions
items.excerpt: Researchers used machine learning to identify a potential precursor signal for sudden stratospheric warming events that disrupt the polar vortex and send frigid air into North America and Europe.

items.title: Researchers develop AI tool to map microRNA binding sites on circular RNAs
items.excerpt: Pusan National University's circMAC predicts where microRNAs bind across full-length circular RNAs at single-nucleotide resolution, outperforming RNA language models in benchmarks (Briefings in Bioinformatics).

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to uncover nearly 10,000 reactions in CO2 conversion, revealing pathways traditional models missed and a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.

history_match.title: Using machine learning and computation to unveil mechanisms for CO2-to-fuel conversion

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: A study finds people rate even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human, though they judge 'awareness' in humans and AI much more similarly.

history_match.title: Even when AI behaves just like us, people still rate it as less conscious than humans

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts; one mathematician called the implications 'staggering.'

history_match.title: AI's failed attempt to crack the Riemann hypothesis led a mathematician to a breakthrough

items.title: Physicists claim they can predict when AI will turn dangerous
items.excerpt: A physics-derived formula tracks an AI model's internal 'compass needle' to flag undesirable outputs before they happen.

history_match.title: Simple math formula predicts when AI chatbots will go rogue

items.title: SEEQC Combines Chip-Based Processing With NVIDIA AI to Improve Quantum Error Correction
items.excerpt: SEEQC reports QEC decoding gains from a multi-stage architecture pairing its on-chip pre-decoder with NVIDIA's Ising open family of AI decoder models.

history_match.title: Riverlane and NVIDIA use AI to speed up quantum decoder calibration

items.title: Study: AI Could Speed Quantum Threats — And Help Build Defenses
items.excerpt: A paper in the Journal of Quantum Information Science argues AI could hasten quantum attacks on encryption while helping organizations prepare, and should be treated with quantum as one security problem.

history_match.title: Riverlane and NVIDIA use AI to speed up quantum decoder calibration

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical computing technique detects deepfake videos with a claimed 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks of similar performance.

history_match.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research details Earth AI geospatial agents that combine Earth-observation foundation models and reasoning to answer complex planetary-scale questions.

history_match.title: Unlocking Earth AI's planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health

items.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
items.excerpt: Google Antigravity serves as an agentic science workbench to discover, structurally evaluate and prioritize novel antimicrobial peptides in hours.

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT historian Benjamin Lindquist argues generative AI is rooted in mid-20th-century engineers' belief that some irrationality was essential for a machine that could think like a human.

items.title: App's AI 'eyes' for blind users fall short, researchers find
items.excerpt: A study of blind users relying on AI visual-assistant apps for everyday tasks like cooking finds the AI descriptions often fall short, forcing repeated queries.

items.title: Yes, AI Is Being Used for Dating Profile Photos
items.excerpt: A psychology blog looks at how AI-generated and AI-enhanced dating profile photos shape impressions, advising users to wait until meeting in person before trusting a photo.

items.title: Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a 'Maths 2.0' world
items.excerpt: Terence Tao argues that as AI tools automatically derive solutions to long-standing problems, mathematics must move to a 'Maths 2.0' era where proof scarcity no longer defines the field and human understanding is prized over publishing more solutions.

history_match.title: The inside story behind OpenAI's million-dollar math proof

items.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
items.excerpt: Viewing diffusion models through Dense Associative Memory theory, the authors show that spurious states, long treated as memory errors, are a critical intermediate phase of generalization, and demonstrate them across many architectures and datasets.

items.title: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models
items.excerpt: The authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within single neurons rather than interactions between neurons, and build a dendrite-inspired model with improved performance.
